title: awk for fields and reports
intro: Work from home. Data files are in **`data/awk/`**. Keep scratch under **`work/`**.

questions.prompt: **`data/awk/queue-times.tsv`** is tab-separated with a header row and two columns: queue name and wait time in minutes. Print each data row with the columns swapped — time first, then queue name — one pair per line.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
awk -F $'\t' 'NR>1 { print $2, $1 }' data/awk/queue-times.tsv
```

`NR>1` skips the header; `$2` and `$1` swap the field order.

questions.prompt: Sum all the wait times in `data/awk/queue-times.tsv`. What is the total?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
awk -F $'\t' 'NR>1 { s += $2 } END { print s+0 }' data/awk/queue-times.tsv
```

questions.prompt: What is the mean wait time across all data rows in `data/awk/queue-times.tsv`, to two decimal places?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
awk -F $'\t' 'NR>1 { s += $2; n++ } END { printf "%.2f\n", s/n }' data/awk/queue-times.tsv
```

questions.prompt: Group the rows of `data/awk/queue-times.tsv` by queue name and compute the total wait time per group. List the results alphabetically by queue name, one `queue total` pair per line.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
awk -F $'\t' 'NR>1 { t[$1] += $2 } END { for (k in t) print k, t[k] }' data/awk/queue-times.tsv | sort
```

`t[$1]` accumulates totals keyed by queue name; `sort` orders the output.

questions.prompt: **`data/awk/tickets.txt`** records ticket IDs and the queue each belongs to. How many tickets belong to each queue? List `queue count` pairs sorted alphabetically.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
awk '{ c[$2]++ } END { for (q in c) print q, c[q] }' data/awk/tickets.txt | sort
```

questions.prompt: **`data/awk/syslog.log`** records system events at different severity levels. Print every line that is an ERROR entry.
questions.expectedOutput:
May 13 ERROR postgres timeout
May 13 ERROR auth lockout
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
awk '/ERROR/' data/awk/syslog.log
```

A bare pattern with no action defaults to `{ print }`.

questions.prompt: **`data/awk/fields.txt`** has lines with varying numbers of space-separated tokens. Print only the lines that contain exactly five tokens.
questions.expectedOutput:
alpha beta gamma delta epsilon
1 2 3 4 5
user id source dest action
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
awk 'NF == 5' data/awk/fields.txt
```

`NF` is the built-in field count for the current record.

questions.prompt: Print each data row from `data/awk/queue-times.tsv` (skip the header) with the queue name left-aligned in 8 characters and the wait time right-aligned in 4 characters, separated by a space.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
awk -F $'\t' 'NR>1 { printf "%-8s %4d\n", $1, $2 }' data/awk/queue-times.tsv
```

`%-8s` left-aligns in 8 chars; `%4d` right-aligns the integer in 4 chars.

questions.prompt: **`data/awk/passwd.sample`** uses the same colon-separated field layout as `/etc/passwd`. Print each entry's login name alongside its home directory, space-separated, one pair per line.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
awk -F ':' '{ print $1, $6 }' data/awk/passwd.sample
```

`/etc/passwd` field order: login:password:uid:gid:gecos:home:shell — home is field 6.

questions.prompt: **`data/awk/queue-names.txt`** maps numeric queue IDs to display names. **`data/awk/queue-codes.txt`** maps the same IDs to short codes. For each entry in `queue-codes.txt`, print the ID, short code, and display name together on one line.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
awk 'FNR==NR { a[$1] = $2; next } { print $1, $2, a[$1] }' data/awk/queue-names.txt data/awk/queue-codes.txt
```

`FNR==NR` is true only while reading the first file — load the ID→name map, then look it up for each row of the second file.

questions.prompt: `/home/isopod/labs/basics/05-awk/transfer-log.csv` records network flows. One transfer stands out as the single largest by bytes — a possible exfiltration event. Find that row. What is its `label` field?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
awk -F, 'NR>1 && $4+0 > max { max=$4+0; label=$5 } END { print label }' /home/isopod/labs/basics/05-awk/transfer-log.csv
```

Track the running maximum in `max`; update `label` whenever a larger value is seen. The `END` block prints the label for the peak transfer row.

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes
- Select and compute on fields with `$N`, `NF`, `NR`, `FNR`.
- Accumulate values in associative arrays; emit in `END`.
- Format output with `printf`; join two files with the `FNR==NR` idiom.

## Scope

**In scope:** `awk` one-liners and short programs for field processing. **Out of scope:** full AWK programs with multiple rules and `BEGIN`/`END` blocks beyond simple aggregation.
